features.feature_value: Tends to remove posts with name-calling/disrespect and is more likely to remove if vulgar language is present.
features.evidence_span: "any post that called anyone names or disrespected someone through name calling should be removed"
features.rationale: The reflection explicitly states a removal rule tied to name-calling/disrespect and vulgarity.

features.feature_value: Allows rude/disrespectful or even cussing content if it is still within speech rights, but removes when disrespect becomes direct/hateful rather than debate.
features.evidence_span: "although what is being said may be rude and disrespectful, it's still valid content for the Freedom to Speak right"
features.rationale: They describe a threshold distinguishing allowable rudeness from unacceptable hateful direct disrespect.

features.feature_value: Uses message tone as a signal; removes or discounts posts that are just bashing, with improper language and fear-mongering rather than a real argument.
features.evidence_span: "I focused more on the tone of the messages"
features.rationale: Their stated approach centers on tone and whether there is an actual argument versus attacks and fear tactics.

features.feature_value: Looks specifically for threatening content and for posts focused on the other side rather than issues.
features.evidence_span: "any threatening content or any that was focused on the other side not just the issues"
features.rationale: They mention two concrete content cues used to judge/remove.

features.feature_value: Decision based on whether content is defamatory, threatening, or excessively negative.
features.rationale: They list the criteria they considered when deciding moderation/retention.

features.feature_value: Criticizes moderation when only one viewpoint is unacceptable; removing both viewpoints is seen as flawed.
features.evidence_span: "deleting both was not a good option"
features.rationale: They address a procedural issue about how pair moderation was applied across viewpoints.

features.feature_value: Reports relying on a mirror test approach and removing feelings rather than personal emotional reaction.
features.evidence_span: "only the mirror test and removing my feelings"
features.rationale: Their reflection describes a specific self-regulation strategy during the task.

features.feature_value: Tries to judge whether content is truly offensive, inflammatory, and dangerous; prefers minimal moderation when such harms are not present.
features.evidence_span: "trying to see if anything was truly offensive, inflammatory, and dangerous"
features.rationale: They state both an assessment threshold and an expressed preference to moderate less when criteria aren’t met.
